outcome_note: Three Gorges Dam combined hydropower and ship locks on the upper Yangtze and was completed in 2012. It also displaced large populations and submerged historic sites, costs Sun's proposal did not mention.

sources.title: Sun Yat-sen, The International Development of China, Program II, Part IV, 1922 edition
Princeton University Art Museum, Three Gorges Dam Migration, historical account of the proposal and completion

claim: Dam the Yangtze rapids for locks and water power

year_made_note: Daedalus lecture delivered to the Cambridge Heretics on 4 February 1923.
who: J. B. S. Haldane, through a fictional future student
quote: It was in 1951 that Dupont and Schwarz produced the first ectogenetic child.
paraphrase: In Daedalus, Haldane's imagined future student records the first child gestated outside any human body in 1951.
outcome_note: No child has been gestated outside a human body. IVF fertilizes eggs in glass and returns them to wombs, and artificial-womb research supports premature infants rather than replacing pregnancy. His date came from an invented student's essay.

sources.title: J. B. S. Haldane, Daedalus, or Science and the Future, 1923
Lancaster University, Ectogenesis: A Retrospective, 2025

claim: The first ectogenetic child produced in 1951

quote: At suitable distances, there will be great power stations where during windy weather the surplus power will be used for the electrolytic decomposition of water into oxygen and hydrogen.
paraphrase: Haldane imagined power stations using surplus wind electricity to split water into hydrogen for storage and later use.
outcome_note: The US National Renewable Energy Laboratory's Wind2H2 project ran wind turbines, electrolysis and hydrogen storage together, proving his mechanism. No national energy system has been built around it, so his vision holds in part.

sources.title: J. B. S. Haldane, Daedalus, or Science and the Future, 1923
NREL, Renewable Hydrogen: Integration, Validation, and Demonstration, 2008
DOE Hydrogen Program, Renewable Electrolysis Integrated Systems Development and Testing, 2012

claim: In windy weather surplus power will split water into hydrogen and oxygen

quote: Broadcasting is a new method likely to acquire great potency as soon as people are satisfied that it is not a method of propaganda.
paraphrase: Russell warned that radio would become a powerful tool of influence once listeners were sure it was not propaganda.
outcome_note: Studies of Weimar and Nazi Germany find radio shifted political support and that Nazi broadcasts fed party recruitment and antisemitic violence. Radio's power is shown; whether trust was the condition for it is not.

sources.title: Bertrand Russell, Icarus, or the Future of Science, 1924, p. 26
Maja Adena and colleagues, Radio and the Rise of the Nazis in Prewar Germany, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130:4 (2015)

claim: Broadcasting will gain great potency once trusted

quote: Three-hour shifts or a fifteen-hour week may put off the problem for a great while. For three hours a day is quite enough to satisfy the old Adam in most of us!
paraphrase: Keynes imagined that by 2030, with far less work needed, people might share it in three-hour shifts or a fifteen-hour week.
outcome_note: Jorg Bibow's 2024 reassessment finds working hours fell but stayed far above fifteen per week. He also notes Keynes offered this figure as possibility, not promise for 2030.

sources.title: John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren, 1930
Jorg Bibow, Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren: 90 Years Later, Levy Economics Institute Working Paper 1038, January 2024

claim: Three-hour shifts or a fifteen-hour week; three hours a day satisfies the old Adam in most of us

quote: This means unemployment due to our discovery of means of economising the use of labour outrunning the pace at which we can find new uses for labour.
paraphrase: Keynes named technological unemployment, where labor-saving inventions displace workers faster than new uses for their labor appear.
outcome_note: Studies of mechanization find long spells of displacement and falling earnings for particular trades, which bears out his mismatch. Keynes called it temporary maladjustment, and how temporary remains open.

sources.title: John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren, 1930
Acemoglu and Johnson, Learning from Ricardo and Thompson

claim: Unemployment comes when we economise labour faster than we find new uses for it

year_made_note: Letter signed in August 1939 and presented to President Roosevelt in October.
role: Physicists warning the U.S. president about nuclear fission
quote: extremely powerful bombs
paraphrase: Einstein, with Leo Szilard, warned President Roosevelt that uranium chain reactions could yield bombs of unprecedented power.
outcome_note: Manhattan Project scientists built these weapons, and their Trinity test on 16 July 1945 set off the first nuclear explosion, six years after this letter.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy, Einstein's Letter, 1939, quoting the letter and describing Szilard's role
U.S. Department of Energy, The Trinity Test, July 16, 1945

claim: Uranium chain reactions could make extremely powerful bombs
